c.pop: 8,900 (combined Windermere & Bowness-on-Windermere civil parish, 2021 census; Windermere town alone: 4,826)
c.tagline: England's largest lake, one grand fell-top view at a time

card: Widely accepted, contactless is standard in shops, cafes, pubs, and even on Windermere Lake Cruises boats. Carry a little cash for rural B&Bs, market stalls, or small fell-side tea rooms.
rides: Local pre-booked taxi firms (Lakes Taxis, Applecabs, Fellrunner Taxis)
Uber/Bolt do not operate in the Lake District

taxi.color: No standard livery, mostly private saloons and estate cars
taxi.fareNote: Most journeys are phone- or app-pre-booked rather than hailed on the street; agree a fixed price for longer runs (e.g., to Kendal or the airport).

emergency.medical: 999 for emergencies; nearest A&E is Westmorland General Hospital, Kendal (about 9 miles away)
emergency.note: Mountain Rescue (Kendal MRT / Langdale-Ambleside MRT) responds to fell and hiking incidents — always dial 999 and ask for Police then Mountain Rescue.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

walk: Bowness-on-Windermere is compact and pedestrian-friendly along the bay, and it connects to Windermere town by a signed 25-30 minute uphill footpath. Beyond the two centers, pavements thin out fast on rural lanes, so sturdy shoes are needed for fell walks, and the terrain is genuinely hilly.

safety.safety: Very safe; Cumbria consistently has one of the lowest crime rates in England and Windermere/Bowness feel comfortable to walk after dark.
safety.crime: Petty theft is the main risk — car break-ins at remote fell-side car parks and unattended bags at busy lake piers in summer. Violent crime is rare. Fell/hiking mishaps are a bigger practical safety concern than crime.

hood_landmark.Bowness-on-Windermere: Bowness Bay piers and Windermere Lake Cruises terminal
hood_landmark.Windermere town: Orrest Head viewpoint and the 1847 railway station
hood_landmark.Storrs / Storrs Park: Storrs Hall and Storrs Temple on the lakeshore

avoid.reason: Occasional car break-ins at remote fell car parks — keep valuables out of sight.

hood_desc: The bustling lakeside hub with the cruise piers, ice cream stalls, pubs and The World of Beatrix Potter — the tourist heart of Windermere.
The quieter hilltop town that grew up around the 1847 railway terminus, with independent shops and cafes and an easy walk up to the classic fell-top view at Orrest Head.
A largely unspoiled Lakeland farming village of slate-roofed cottages strung along a valley just north of Windermere, home to the historic Townend farmhouse.
A lively outdoor-adventure town at the lake's northern tip, packed with hiking-gear shops, cafes and waterfall walks, a short bus or boat ride from Bowness.
A genteel, wooded stretch of lakeshore south of Bowness lined with grand Victorian hotels and historic estates, good for a quiet lakeside stroll away from the crowds.

water.note: UK tap water is safe to drink everywhere.

transit.sys: Windermere Lake Cruises ferry network plus Stagecoach Cumbria buses; no local rail beyond the Windermere branch-line terminus
transit.hours: Cruises run roughly 9:45am–5:30pm; buses generally run about 7am–11pm
transit.pay: Buses: tap card or cash on board; cruises: buy at the pier kiosk or online. Day passes exist for both.
transit.map: Route maps posted at Windermere Lake Cruises piers and on the Stagecoach Cumbria and Traveline websites
transit.note: A separate small car-and-passenger chain ferry crosses the lake year-round at Ferry Nab to Far Sawrey — handy for reaching Hill Top and Hawkshead without driving around the lake.

transport.air: Nearest airport is Manchester Airport (MAN), about 90 miles away; Liverpool John Lennon and Newcastle are secondary options.
transport.train: Windermere railway station is the terminus of a branch line with roughly hourly trains to/from Manchester Airport and Manchester Piccadilly (about 2 hours); London Euston connects via Oxenholme on the West Coast Main Line in about 3.5–4 hours.
transport.bus: National Express coaches link major UK cities to Kendal/Windermere; local Stagecoach Cumbria buses connect Windermere/Bowness with Ambleside, Grasmere, Kendal and the wider national park.
transport.ferry: No international ferry service; Windermere Lake Cruises and the small Ferry Nab car ferry handle only on-lake, local travel.
transport.car: Via the M6 (Junction 36) then the A591, about 2.5–3 hours from Manchester or Liverpool. Parking in central Bowness and Windermere is limited and expensive in peak season.

airport.name: Manchester Airport
airport.distance: About 90 miles / 145 km (roughly 2–2.5 hours by train or car)
airport.transport: Direct or one-change trains run from Manchester Airport station to Windermere roughly hourly (~2 hours); pre-booked private transfers cost roughly $180–250 one-way and take about 2 hours

net.m: 4G is generally reliable in the Bowness and Windermere town centers but drops out frequently on fells, in valleys, and around villages like Troutbeck; 5G coverage is limited.
net.w: Free Wi-Fi is common in cafes, pubs and hotels in town; coverage is patchier at rural attractions and on the trails.
net.gb: About $15–25 for a 15–20GB tourist SIM or eSIM
net.fwn: Most cafes, hotels and the Brockhole National Park Visitor Centre offer free Wi-Fi to customers
net.ap: SIM cards available at Manchester Airport and phone shops in Windermere/Ambleside; eSIMs can be activated before arrival

tip.s: Tipping is not obligatory anywhere in the UK. Rounding up a taxi fare or leaving small change at a cafe is appreciated but not expected.
tip.r: In restaurants and pubs with table service, 10–12.5% is typical if a service charge isn't already added to the bill.
